predecessors.note: The rus dossier draws Tmutarakan inside Kievan Rus' from 990 to 1054 (Mstislav was its prince 'in or after 988'); this dossier takes over at the division.

capitals.name: Tmutarakan (Taman)
capitals.note: The infobox gives no capital; the town on the Taman peninsula is the seat.

correction.text: the Taman peninsula and the Strait of Kerch, where, the page says, it controlled the Cimmerian Bosporus

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Cliopatria has no Tmutarakan row; its 1236 Rus shape is a 1,068 km2 fragment on the Taman peninsula (the rus dossier marks it wrong). The pages give no area and no boundary; Taman plus the Kerch strait is my reading of where, the page says, it controlled the Cimmerian Bosporus (Tmutarakan page) and 'controlling the Strait of Kerch' (Mstislav page).

region.text: the Taman peninsula and the Strait of Kerch, where, the page says, it controlled the Cimmerian Bosporus

ledger.note: (Confidence 2, reviewer eu-16-x: the Kievan Rus' page lists the division without a year; 1054 is Yaroslav's death.) 1054: Tmutarakan goes to Sviatoslav II with Chernigov. The division gives 'Principality of Chernigov and Tmutarakan, for Sviatoslav II of Kiev'; the page also says it was 'the Black Sea port of Tmutarakan belonging to Chernigov'. The Mstislav page's infobox ends the earlier principality 'united with Kievan Rus' (from 1054 Sviatoslav I)'. The principality is drawn separately because Chernigov's dossier does not draw it.

region.text: the Taman peninsula and the Strait of Kerch, where, the page says, it controlled the Cimmerian Bosporus

ledger.note: 1094: Oleg Sviatoslavich leaves Tmutarakan for Chernigov. 'in 1094, he returned from Tmutarakan with an armed force of Kipchaks to Rus', drove out Monomakh and captured Chernigov.' None of the four pages dates the end of Rus rule at Tmutarakan (the Tmutarakan page: Byzantine 'more direct rule for a while', then Trebizond in the 13th century, Genoa in the 14th), so 1094 is a bridge, confidence 1.

wars.name: Rostislav Vladimirovich's seizure of Tmutarakan
wars.outcome: 'In 1064 he was displaced by the rival Rus prince Rostislav Vladimirovich' (Gleb Svyatoslavich); Rostislav was poisoned on 3 February 1066 by a Byzantine envoy from Chersonesos. A change of prince, not of border.
wars.note: In 1079 Svyatoslav Yaroslavich appointed a governor, who was captured two years later; Oleg 'returned to Tmutarakan in 1083' (Tmutarakan page). Oleg had fled there on 10 April 1077 (Oleg page).

certainty.note: A trading town and its strait; no boundary on any page.

sources.title: Tmutarakan
sources.note: Rus control from the late 10th century, princes 1064-1094, later Byzantine, Trebizond and Genoese rule; no area, no capital.

sources.title: Mstislav of Chernigov
sources.note: Appointed to Tmutarakan in or after 988; controlling the Strait of Kerch; 1029 Alans; died c. 1035; infobox successor 1054.

sources.title: Oleg I of Chernigov
sources.note: Fled to Tmutarakan on 10 April 1077; left for Chernigov in 1094; silent on who held it afterwards.

sources.title: Kievan Rus'
sources.note: The 1054 division: Chernigov and Tmutarakan for Sviatoslav II; silent on its end.

notes: New state flagged by eu-16-b (Chernigov), counterpart 'Tmutarakan', 1054. Start is the 1054 division because the rus dossier draws Tmutarakan from 990 to 1054; the Chernigov dossier does not draw it, so without this dossier the strait is blank 1054-1094. A reviewer may prefer to fold it into principality-of-chernigov as a region. End 1094 is a confidence-1 bridge: Oleg left in 1094, but no page opened dates the loss of Tmutarakan (the Cumans, Byzantium and Khazars are not dated by these pages; the Tmutarakan page says only 'more direct rule for a while' by Byzantium). successors left empty for that reason: Byzantine rule, then the Empire of Trebizond (13th century) and Genoa (14th), all undated here. Mstislav's 1022 duel with the Kassogian Rededia and his 1029 suzerainty over the Alans of the lower Don belong to the rus period (before 1054) and are not entered. Wikidata id unknown. Page budget used: four pages.
